jobs.prompt: Fix the Sonnet review findings on the process-control part of the batch (tools/server-restart.mjs, tools/update-pending.mjs, tools/watch-cli.mjs, tools/watch-server.mjs, the wiring in tools/swarm/core-52.mjs). HIGH (1) pid identity: before sending SIGTERM to a recorded pid verify it is still the same server: the process command line (ps -o command= -p PID on macOS and Linux, argument array, no shell) must contain the swarm runner and the recorded subcommand (watch or remote serve), and its start time (ps -o lstart= or etimes, converted) must not be later than the record startedAt plus 5 seconds; if the check cannot be made or does not match, do NOT signal, report the stale record (remove it when the pid is dead or belongs to something else) and say so in the output. MEDIUM (2) spawn: attach an error handler to the replacement spawn, validate cwd exists and is a directory before stopping the old server, and decide to stop the old server only after the replacement command is known to be startable (runner file exists, cwd exists, argv is an array of strings); write the report lines as they happen, never only at the end, so a crash cannot lose them. (3) A failed restart (old server stopped, replacement not up) is reported loudly and the update exit code stays 0 but the JSON servers entry has status failed and the human output ends with the exact manual command; a port that is not an integer from 1 to 65535 makes that server a reported failure, never an exception. (4) The runner path: resolve the install root the same way the update flow does (the installed current runner, not the checkout root); when current does not exist fall back to the runner of the version just installed under versions, and if neither exists report and do not stop the server. (5) update-pending: a corrupt or unreadable pending record is treated as stale: removed with a warning, never thrown from readLivePending; registration of held pids is serialized with a small lock or an atomic append so a registration is never lost; the update must not wait for a process that only waits for the update: a busy marker whose pid is a held launcher or an ancestor of one is ignored, and a wave loop (go scope) or autopilot that is itself held is not counted as busy; the hold expiry is extended (refreshed) while the update is actively waiting or running its update steps, so launchers are never released mid-checkout; createOnly becomes an atomic exclusive create (link or open with the exclusive flag), and SIGTERM and SIGHUP remove the record. (6) manualCommand never prints environment variable values (print only the variable names, or nothing); the recorded env subset is not shown. (7) registryEnv keeps SWARM_BOARD_FILE and SWARM_REMOTE_SERVER_FILE so servers using custom record files are found. LOW (8) a recorded argv has --open removed on restart so a restart never reopens a browser; a board started from a terminal with redirected output is only classed background when a TTY check on stdin AND stdout both fail and the record says so explicitly; /api/health answers only for a loopback socket with a loopback Host header and returns only version and pid. Add a test for each numbered point in tests/server-restart-review.test.mjs and tests/update-pending-review.test.mjs. Keep every existing test passing (change a test only where a finding changes intended behavior, with a comment). Do not edit tools/swarm.mjs unless a call site must pass a new option (then change only that call). Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Tests are hermetic (no ambient environment, no TTY, no network). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.

Fix the Sonnet review findings on the registry, scratch and hook part of the batch (tools/projects.mjs, tools/scratch-roots.mjs, tools/handbuild.mjs, tools/handbuild-commands.mjs, tools/board-inbox.mjs, tools/githook-check.mjs, tools/git-hooks.mjs). HIGH (1) The registry reader that prunes missing folders must never drop a project because of a stat error that is not ENOENT or ENOTDIR (EACCES, EIO, ETIMEDOUT, a hung or unmounted network share): such entries are kept and reported as unreachable; prune only on ENOENT or ENOTDIR and only when the parent of the root exists and is readable (an unmounted volume has no parent mount); the stat of each entry has a 2 second timeout and the loop runs the stats concurrently so one hung mount cannot hang the board; pruning is never done when the registry file itself looks damaged. (2) Split the classifier into two functions in tools/scratch-roots.mjs: isScratchRoot (STRICT, used by the owner inbox, the phone, swarm-inbox, the handbuild auto-deny and swarm forget --scratch: only the scratch base ~/.project-swarm-scratch and its worktrees, the OS temp folders, folders whose name starts with .tmp-test, a pointer with scratch true, and the .swarm-scratch marker) and isTestTempRoot (BROAD, used only for hiding projects in the default board listing: strict rules OR a path segment exactly tmp, temp, test, tests or __tests__, case-insensitive); a real project under a folder named test or Temp must never lose its inbox items or have a request auto-denied; update every caller accordingly and say so in the module header. (3) The commit-msg hook: it must never lock anyone out of committing because of infrastructure: if node cannot be found (try the recorded node path from install time first, then PATH), the check script is missing, or the check throws or times out (5 seconds), the hook prints a one-line warning to stderr and exits 0; only a positive violation exits non-zero. The recorded node path and check path are single-quoted with embedded single quotes escaped (never double-quoted JSON strings) so dollar signs and backticks in an install path cannot expand. MEDIUM (4) Overwriting: if a .before-swarm backup already exists and the current hook is not ours, write the new backup under a unique name (.before-swarm-2, and so on) and chain the most recent one; never overwrite a user hook without a backup; also set the executable bit on an existing non-executable hook of ours and refuse to write through a symlink (replace it). (5) The subject rule matches only subjects of the form Manifest: or Manifests: or Manifest for (case-insensitive, at the start of the first non-comment line), not ordinary subjects such as Manifest parser: fix; merge commits (MERGE_HEAD present) and fixup or squash or amend-without-new-message flows are skipped; names are read with git diff --cached --name-status -z --no-renames so quoted non-ASCII paths and the diff.renames setting do not matter (a rename shows as a delete plus an add, both names count); a subject line starting with a hash character is a comment only when it is preceded by the comment character git is configured with (default hash) and the message came from an editor; paths are compared case-sensitively under coordination/manifests/. (6) SWARM_SCRATCH_BASE is validated: it must be an absolute path that is not the root, not the home folder, not an ancestor of the home folder and not inside a registered real project; an invalid value is ignored with a warning and the default is used; the empty string means unset. (7) ownerInboxContext no longer sniffs new Error().stack: the callers pass an explicit option (forOwner: true) from the board server, the phone and swarm-inbox code paths (find them: tools/board-inbox.mjs callers, the inbox collect step in tools/inbox.mjs, tools/phone.mjs and the watch server), and the registry reader prunes and filters only when that option is true. (8) The registry read-modify-write (forget, add, prune, lastSeen touch) takes a cross-process lock (mkdir-based, stale after 30 seconds, owner pid) and re-reads inside the lock; a failed prune write never overwrites a registry that was damaged on read (keep the original); the write uses a temp file in the same folder, fsync, rename, cleans the temp file on failure and keeps a symlinked registry as a symlink (write through to its target). (9) forget refuses the install root also when installRoot is not passed (resolve it from the install location); one install-root hit in a bulk run is reported and skipped, never aborting the rest; --dry-run on a damaged registry prints the damage error. (10) A chained .before-swarm pre-push hook receives the stdin lines (tee them to a temp file and feed both). LOW (11) auto-deny prints the request id, the reason scratch project, and how to turn it off (move the project out of the scratch base or remove the marker); the request is created already denied in one atomic write; board-inbox phone-state counts exclude scratch projects; forget --scratch and the inbox use the same strict function with the same installRoot argument. Add a test for each numbered point in tests/registry-review.test.mjs, tests/scratch-strict-broad.test.mjs and tests/commit-msg-review.test.mjs. Keep every existing test passing (change a test only where a finding changes intended behavior, with a comment). Do not edit tools/swarm.mjs unless a call site must pass a new option (then change only that call). Never import install.mjs statically from new modules. Tests are hermetic (no ambient environment, no TTY, no network). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only the named files and their tests change.
